tour.name: Uluru & Kata Tjuta Private 3-Day Tour: Sunrise, Sunset, the Base Walk & the Field of Light
tour.subtitle: Three days in Australia's Red Centre with a private guide: sunset and sunrise at Uluru, the base walk to the Mutitjulu waterhole and its rock art, the domes of Kata Tjuta and the Valley of the Winds, the Field of Light and a dinner under the desert stars.

tour.overview:
In the heart of Australia, Uluru rises 348 metres from the red desert plain, a single sandstone monolith that changes colour with the light. Thirty kilometres away, the 36 domes of Kata Tjuta form a maze of gorges. Both are sacred to the Anangu people, the traditional owners, whose culture here is among the oldest living cultures in the world; the national park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for both nature and culture, and climbing Uluru has been banned since 2019 out of respect.

This private three-day tour shows the Red Centre with a private guide: the rock at sunset and sunrise, the base walks, Kata Tjuta, the Field of Light and a dinner under the stars, with two nights at Ayers Rock Resort.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: 3 days, 2 nights
• Start and end: Ayers Rock airport
• Type: private tour with guide and vehicle; 2 nights with breakfast
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability, your hotel and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; walks of up to 7 kilometres

WHAT YOU SEE
• Uluru at sunset and sunrise.
• The Mala and Kuniya walks and the Mutitjulu waterhole.
• The Cultural Centre.
• Kata Tjuta and the Valley of the Winds.
• The Field of Light.

WHY THIS WORKS
Three days allow sunrise and sunset at both sites and walks in the cooler early mornings, with a guide who explains Anangu culture.

WHO IT SUITS
Nature lovers, walkers, photographers and families.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To include Kings Canyon, ask us for a 4-day version.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Summer days (December to February) can exceed 40°C; walks start at dawn. Fly nets are useful from spring to autumn. Park passes are required.

days.name: Arrival, the Cultural Centre and sunset at Uluru
days.description:
What to expect: a first look at Uluru and its culture.

Your guide meets you at Ayers Rock airport and takes you to your hotel at the resort. In the afternoon you visit the Uluru-Kata Tjuta Cultural Centre, where the Anangu explain Tjukurpa, the law and stories that link the people to the land, and walk the Kuniya walk to the Mutitjulu waterhole, a permanent water source with rock art. At sunset, you watch Uluru turn from orange to deep red, with drinks and canapés.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
Afternoon – Arrival and check-in.
15:30 – Cultural Centre.
16:30 – Kuniya walk and Mutitjulu waterhole.
18:00 – Sunset at Uluru with drinks.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Some sacred sites must not be photographed; signs indicate them.

INCLUDED: transfers, guide, park pass, sunset drinks.
NOT INCLUDED: dinner.

Overnight: Ayers Rock Resort.
Meals: canapés.

days.name: Sunrise at Kata Tjuta, the Valley of the Winds, and the Field of Light
days.description:
What to expect: the domes of Kata Tjuta and an evening of desert lights.

You leave before dawn to watch the sunrise over Kata Tjuta, with Uluru on the horizon, then walk into the Valley of the Winds, a trail of about 7 kilometres between the great red domes to the Karu and Karingana lookouts. In the afternoon you rest at the resort. After dark, you walk among the Field of Light, an installation by the artist Bruce Munro of some 50,000 solar-powered lights that bloom slowly in changing colours, followed by a three-course dinner under the stars, with a guide pointing out the constellations of the southern sky.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:30 – Drive to Kata Tjuta.
06:30 – Sunrise.
07:15 – Valley of the Winds walk.
11:00 – Back at the resort.
19:00 – Field of Light.
19:45 – Dinner under the stars.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Valley of the Winds trail closes at 11:00 on hot days.
• Walpa Gorge is an easier alternative.

INCLUDED: guide, vehicle, Field of Light, dinner.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch.

Overnight: Ayers Rock Resort.
Meals: breakfast, dinner.

days.name: Sunrise at Uluru, the base walk and departure
days.description:
What to expect: Uluru at dawn and up close.

You watch the sun rise over Uluru from the Talinguru Nyakunytjaku viewing area, then walk the Mala walk with your guide, past caves with rock art and the Kantju Gorge, or the full base walk of about 10 kilometres around the rock if you prefer. After breakfast, you are taken to the airport for your flight.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:30 – Sunrise at Uluru.
07:00 – Mala walk or full base walk.
10:00 – Breakfast.
12:00 – Airport transfer.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Book a flight from 13:00 onwards.

INCLUDED: guide, vehicle, transfer.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch.

Overnight: none.
Meals: breakfast.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability, hotels and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we climb Uluru?
faq.answer: No. The climb was permanently closed in 2019 at the request of the Anangu.

faq.question: How do we get to Uluru?
faq.answer: By direct flights to Ayers Rock airport from Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane and other cities.

faq.question: What kind of hotel is used?
faq.answer: A comfortable hotel at Ayers Rock Resort; Longitude 131° can be booked for luxury.

faq.question: How hot is it?
faq.answer: From December to February, often over 40°C; from June to August, days are mild and nights cold.

faq.question: Are there flies?
faq.answer: From spring to autumn, bush flies can be persistent: a fly net is a good idea.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Walks can be shortened. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. Viewing areas and parts of the base walk are accessible.

faq.question: Can we add a helicopter flight?
faq.answer: Yes, over Uluru and Kata Tjuta at sunrise or sunset.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light, covering clothes, a hat, sun cream, sturdy shoes and warm layers for the evenings.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: May to September, when days are cooler.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not expected in Australia, where wages are higher, but it is always appreciated for excellent service.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 30 days before the tour starts. Flights and the dinner under the stars may have stricter terms; we explain them when we confirm. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
